place.name: Nairobi street economy & parallel rails
place.summary: Two economies in one city: the CBD's matatus, hawkers and street food; and Kibera's Bitcoin circular economy. Underneath both, water cuts, drainage warnings and civic pressure.

stories.text:
Ate kebabs and smocha in the streets of Kanairo today. 😊
The economy may be winning.
The rent may be plotting.
But for a brief moment, standing on a Nairobi street with a smocha in one hand and absolutely no financial solutions in the other...
life was good. 😭🌭

Nairobi CBD is a very strange place.
You'll almost get hit by a bus, buy socks, hear three different preachers, dodge ten hawkers and witness a minor crime...
all before lunch. 😭💀

The boy is back from Nairobi CBD. 😭
I have seen things.
I have boarded matatus.
I have crossed roads with a survival rate of 50%.
I have witnessed economic activity beyond human comprehension.
I am tired. 💀

The boy is headed to Nairobi CBD for a few errands. 🇰🇪
Pray for me.
Not because the errands are difficult.
Because Nairobi has a way of introducing new expenses you never planned for. 😭💔💀

What does bitcoin feel like when it's the only door?

In the West we weigh it against SpaceX or index funds.

In Nairobi, with a smartphone, it's the ONLY asset you can own.

Not a portfolio choice.

A whole generation walking through one door.

https://vod.ageofabundance.live/ep-068/clips/x-clip-15-the-young-person-in-nairobi-who-only-knows-bitcoin.mp4

🎙️ FROM THE FOUNDER’S DESK | EPISODE 4

What happens when Bitcoin is built around real community needs?

In Episode 4, we sit down with Ronnie Mdawida, Founder of AfriBit Kibera. 🇰🇪 

We explore how AfriBit Kibera is building a Bitcoin circular economy in Kibera, Nairobi.

We discuss:
🔸  Ronnie’s Bitcoin journey: How he discovered Bitcoin in 2019. And how it changed his view of money.

♻️ Building around community needs: Waste management. Youth opportunities. Local businesses. Savings.

🔸 Bitcoin and Lightning: How Lightning helps make small payments easier and more practical.

🤝 Building trus

"There's a whole community in Kibera that uses Bitcoin day-to-day, and you will never see that business come across to you..."

Robert Kirubi recently explained to a banker in Kenya that members of the nostr:nprofile1qqsxetyf346j86t4st0vrp9ekq8vwzxc4u7hepnpn3zuafr83wctctqpz3mhxue69uhhyetvv9ujuetcd96zuur4vgq3vamnwvaz7tmjv4kxz7fwwpexjmtpdshxuet5ajtzd2 community have been using bitcoin as everyday money for years now
https://v.nostr.build/BTPhhRsPOoaHG0hIoHZStj.mp4

Blink brought the BTC Map merchant directory inside the wallet this week — on a shared open standard other wallets are adopting too, so finding where to spend Bitcoin no longer means leaving the app.

In Nairobi, one settlement reported 3.78M sats circulating locally across 11 projects. BTCPay shipped a Core Lightning update but kept external access disabled while it recovers. And a reported crackdown in Afghanistan was a reminder that where Bitcoin gets banned, it's often needed most.

amendments.sig-infra: The water cut is scheduled maintenance, not failure — but 26 hours is still 26 hours.

interventions.name: Nairobi water & drainage programme
interventions.note: County maintenance and El Niño preparedness — scheduled but leaving 17 neighbourhoods dry for 26 hours.

interventions.name: Kibera circular-economy rails
interventions.note: AfriBit, Dada Devs, BTC Map merchants — a parallel economy the banking system can't see.

sips.title: The parallel rails are the hedge
sips.what_changes: When 17 neighbourhoods lose water and the CBD runs on hustle, the sats economy in Kibera is a working fallback — invisible to the formal system.

sips.title: The 26-hour water test
sips.what_changes: If scheduled cuts stretch or repeat, water becomes the city's binding constraint before drainage fails in the rains.
